approaches.name: Lateral MIPO approach to the distal femur
approaches.corridor: Short distal lateral window, sub-vastus-lateralis plate tunnel, proximal window, and percutaneous screw portals

sources.title: MIPO Approach To The Distal Femur From Lateral Anterolateral
Minimally Invasive Plate Osteosynthesis for Periprosthetic and Interprosthetic Fractures Associated with Knee Arthroplasty
Current concepts in the treatment of distal femur fractures in adults

procedure_applications.condition: A bridge-plating strategy can preserve the metaphyseal soft-tissue envelope while indirect reduction restores length, alignment, and rotation

positioning.text: Position supine on a radiolucent table with the knee flexed enough for reduction and unobstructed full-length AP and lateral imaging.

setup.text: Template plate length, reduction aids, distal and proximal windows, and every percutaneous screw trajectory before tunneling; prepare to enlarge the exposure if reduction is unacceptable.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark lateral epicondyle, joint line, patella, Gerdy tubercle, femoral shaft axis, and greater trochanter.

incision.text: Use a shortened distal lateral incision beginning in the metaphyseal region; extend to Gerdy tubercle only when arthrotomy is required, plus a proximal window and 1-1.5 cm screw portals.

superficial_interval.text: Split iliotibial band with its fibers distally and open fascia lata and vastus-lateralis fascia through the proximal window.

deep_interval.text: Leave vastus lateralis largely undisturbed, create a submuscular extraperiosteal tunnel, slide the plate along lateral femur, and bluntly split proximal muscle fibers only for plate control.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue, iliotibial band or fascia lata, vastus-lateralis fascia and fibers at windows, submuscular plane, then lateral femur.

structures_encountered.text: Iliotibial band, vastus lateralis, lateral genicular branches, lateral capsule when opened, and lateral femoral cortex are encountered.

structures_at_risk.text: Superior lateral genicular vessels, profunda perforators proximally, periosteal blood supply, patellar tendon, lateral meniscus, and posterior neurovascular structures are at risk.

danger_zones.text: Do not pass the plate, drill, or retractors blindly off bone posteriorly; maintain bony contact and controlled depth throughout tunneling and screw placement.

retraction_hazards.text: Avoid excessive patellar-tendon tension during arthrotomy and avoid posterior Hohmann placement beyond direct bony control.

exposure.text: Provides distal reduction and plate control while preserving the intervening muscle and fracture biology; optional limited arthrotomy visualizes the joint.

limitations.text: Indirect visualization increases malalignment and malposition risk; complex articular reduction must be completed directly before bridge plating.

extensions.text: Lengthen the distal window for arthrotomy, enlarge proximal or screw windows, or convert to open lateral/parapatellar exposure when reduction or plate position cannot be verified.

indications.text: Use for extra-articular, metaphyseal, and selected reconstructed intra-articular distal-femur fractures suited to biological bridge plating.

relative_contraindications.text: Avoid as a purely percutaneous strategy when articular reduction, debridement, vascular repair, or alignment cannot be obtained and confirmed indirectly.

implant_implications.text: Center a sufficiently long lateral plate distally and proximally before sequential fixation; preserve working length and verify every percutaneous screw path.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Confirm length, rotation, mechanical axis, condylar width, plate centering, and screw containment on full-length AP, lateral, and oblique views before locking the construct.

closure.text: Repair any arthrotomy and close iliotibial band or fascia at every window, then close subcutaneous tissue and skin.

complications.text: Complications include malalignment, plate or screw malposition, neurovascular injury, nonunion, infection, stiffness, and fixation failure.

bailouts.text: If indirect reduction or implant placement remains uncertain, enlarge or convert the approach and obtain direct control rather than accepting an unverified construct.

questions.question: Where is the plate passed?
questions.answer: In the natural submuscular plane beneath vastus lateralis.

questions.question: When is a distal arthrotomy added?
questions.answer: When the articular surface requires direct visualization.

questions.question: What must be confirmed before proximal screws?
questions.answer: Central proximal plate position on the femoral shaft.

approaches.name: Safe corridors for temporary distal-femur spanning external fixation
approaches.region: femoral shaft, knee, and tibial shaft
approaches.corridor: Anterior-to-lateral femoral shaft and anteromedial tibial shaft percutaneous pin corridors

sources.title: Minimally Invasive Plate Osteosynthesis for Periprosthetic and Interprosthetic Fractures Associated with Knee Arthroplasty

procedure_applications.condition: Temporary knee-spanning fixation is required while preserving future definitive surgical corridors

positioning.text: Position supine with the entire injured limb accessible and imageable from proximal femur through tibia.

setup.text: Map soft-tissue injury and future plate or nail paths first; place femoral pins in the proximal third and tibial pins in midshaft when later conversion is anticipated.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark femoral shaft, quadriceps envelope, patella, fibular head, tibial crest, and planned definitive incisions.

incision.text: Use adequate small incisions for blunt dissection to bone rather than driving pins directly through tethered skin.

superficial_interval.text: Femoral pins pass through anterior rectus split or direct lateral vastus; tibial pins begin about 1 cm medial to the crest on the anteromedial surface.

deep_interval.text: Advance drill guides to bone, drill bicortically without plunging, and keep the tibial trajectory approximately 20 degrees from sagittal away from posterolateral structures.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue, quadriceps or vastus lateralis to femur; skin and subcutaneous tissue directly to anteromedial tibia.

structures_encountered.text: Rectus femoris or vastus lateralis, femoral cortex, tibial crest, and anteromedial tibial cortex are encountered.

structures_at_risk.text: Sciatic nerve, femoral and popliteal vessels, common and deep peroneal nerves, anterior tibial vessels, saphenous nerve, and future surgical planes are at risk.

danger_zones.text: Avoid medial/posterior femoral trajectories, the fibular-head peroneal-nerve zone, and posterolateral tibial drilling toward the anterior tibial bundle.

retraction_hazards.text: Avoid soft-tissue tethering around pins and thermal or plunge injury during drilling; use sleeves, irrigation, and controlled bicortical depth.

exposure.text: Provides safe percutaneous skeletal purchase for a knee-spanning frame while keeping traumatized and definitive operative zones clear.

limitations.text: Safe zones are corridor guides, not substitutes for patient-specific imaging, palpation, soft-tissue assessment, or direct technique.

extensions.text: Add pins only after remapping neurovascular and definitive implant corridors; do not crowd the future operative field.

indications.text: Use for staged temporary stabilization of unstable distal-femur injuries with soft-tissue compromise or physiologic need for damage control.

relative_contraindications.text: Avoid crushed, infected, burned, or planned-incision skin and any corridor whose anatomy cannot be confidently defined.

implant_implications.text: Keep pins outside the future nail path and plate footprint and sufficiently distant from fracture and definitive incisions.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Confirm bicortical purchase, pin trajectory, joint clearance, and frame alignment without drill plunge.

closure.text: Release tethered skin around each pin, dress pin sites, and document neurovascular status after frame assembly.

complications.text: Complications include neurovascular injury, pin-track infection, thermal necrosis, fracture propagation, joint penetration, stiffness, and contamination of definitive fixation corridors.

bailouts.text: If the safe corridor or future plan is uncertain, stop and relocate under imaging or direct exposure rather than accept a hazardous pin.

questions.question: What is the safest femoral arc?
Where should tibial pins begin?
questions.answer: About 1 cm medial to the tibial crest on the anteromedial surface.

questions.question: Why keep pins away from future fixation?
questions.answer: To avoid contaminating or obstructing definitive plate or nail corridors.

approaches.name: Swashbuckler approach to the distal femur
approaches.corridor: Anterior skin incision with lateral parapatellar arthrotomy and vastus-lateralis mobilization that preserves quadriceps muscle bellies

sources.title: The swashbuckler: a modified anterior approach for fractures of the distal femur
Swashbuckler approach for distal femur fractures: A systematic review

procedure_applications.condition: A complex articular distal-femur fracture requires broad anterior visualization while preserving quadriceps muscle bellies
A lateral Hoffa fragment is amenable to posterior lag-screw fixation through the modified anterior exposure

positioning.text: Position supine on a radiolucent table with the knee flexed and the limb mobile for patellar displacement and fluoroscopy.

setup.text: Review CT-defined articular fragments and prepare independent lag-screw and lateral plate strategies before exposure.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark patella, patellar tendon, tibial tubercle, lateral joint line, lateral epicondyle, and femoral shaft.

incision.text: Use an anterior longitudinal incision compatible with broad distal-femur access and possible future knee arthroplasty.

superficial_interval.text: Develop the lateral parapatellar side while preserving quadriceps muscle bellies and mobilizing the extensor mechanism as a controlled unit.

deep_interval.text: Open the lateral parapatellar capsule and elevate or mobilize vastus lateralis to expose the entire articular surface and lateral distal femur.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue, lateral retinacular-capsular layer, vastus-lateralis interface, synovium, then distal femoral articular surface.

structures_encountered.text: Extensor mechanism, patella, lateral retinaculum, vastus lateralis, femoral condyles, trochlea, and lateral femoral cortex are encountered.

structures_at_risk.text: Patellar tendon, articular cartilage, menisci, genicular vessels, vastus-lateralis blood supply, and posterior neurovascular structures during posterior drilling are at risk.

danger_zones.text: Posterior-to-anterior Hoffa drilling points toward the popliteal fossa; use direct fragment control, guarded drilling, and fluoroscopy.

retraction_hazards.text: Avoid forceful extensor-mechanism retraction and focal patellar cartilage pressure; extend exposure instead of levering through a short arthrotomy.

exposure.text: Exposes the entire distal-femoral articular surface and lateral metaphysis while sparing quadriceps muscle bellies.

limitations.text: Posterior medial fragments and vascular injuries may require separate fragment-specific or medial/posterior access.

extensions.text: Extend proximally along lateral femur for plate application or add a fragment-specific medial/posterior window when anterior visualization is insufficient.

indications.text: Use for complex complete-articular distal-femur fractures and selected lateral Hoffa injuries requiring broad articular visualization.

relative_contraindications.text: Choose a smaller lateral/MIPO approach when broad articular exposure is unnecessary and a targeted posterior route when the critical fragment remains unseen.

implant_implications.text: Supports direct articular lag-screw reconstruction followed by lateral plating; posterior screw trajectories require strict neurovascular safeguards.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Verify articular congruity, alignment, plate position, and posterior lag-screw length on AP, lateral, notch, and oblique views.

closure.text: Repair capsule and lateral retinaculum, restore extensor-mechanism tracking, achieve hemostasis, and close in layers.

complications.text: Complications include stiffness, extensor dysfunction, articular malreduction, neurovascular injury, infection, nonunion, malalignment, and post-traumatic arthritis.

bailouts.text: Add a fragment-specific exposure if posterior reduction or safe screw placement cannot be seen; never drill blindly toward the popliteal fossa.

questions.question: What is the principal exposure advantage?
questions.answer: Visualization of the entire distal-femoral articular surface.
